$comment: Hand-maintained inventory of every data item the AI Code Feedback system collects or derives. Source of truth for the documentation site. See scripts/check.mjs.

tables.what: One row per student account. Created by a trigger on auth.users.
Every consent answer, with the version of the consent text.
One row per sign-in or restore in one VS Code window, with activity counters merged every 3 minutes.
One row per help request (one call to explain), including cache hits.
Research events: one row per observed occurrence, with a JSON payload of derived measurements.
Shared cache of generated hint ladders, keyed by a content hash. No user id.
tables.rls: select where course_id is null (all rows)

tables.what: Per-student summaries written by the model, and the counter that decides when to rewrite them.
Requests and tokens per student per UTC hour, for the rate limit.
At most one row with the hourly and daily request limits set in the dashboard.
Reference table from the base schema. Never read or written by any code.
Dashboard accounts (admin or viewer). Not Supabase Auth users.
Dashboard sign-in sessions (SHA-256 of the token, 12 h).
Dashboard activity log: sign-ins, exports and every change to student data or accounts.

dropped.object: interactions.followup_count, still_confused_count, resolved, resolved_at, time_to_first_edit_ms, concepts_requested

items.name: Student id (UUID)
items.collection: Copied from auth.users.id by the trigger handle_new_user when the account is created.

items.name: Username
items.allowed: 3-32 characters, pattern ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{2,31}$ (checked by the extension only); unique; cannot change
items.collection: Typed by the student at first sign-in. Sign-in fails for an unknown username, so the extension registers it at once. The trigger copies it from the sign-up metadata.

items.name: Display name
items.collection: Declared in the base schema. No code writes it.

items.name: Interface language
items.collection: Declared in the base schema. No code writes it, so it keeps its default. The dashboard shows it in the student detail.

items.name: Feedback language
items.collection: Chosen by the student in the sidebar (before sign-in) or with the globe button (after sign-in). Also sets the interface language of the extension.

items.name: First sign-in time
items.collection: Set by the extension at the first successful sign-in.

items.name: Consent status
items.missing: pending = the student has not answered yet
items.collection: Written by the extension when the student answers the consent dialog (I agree / No thanks). Closing the dialog keeps it pending.

items.name: Consent time
items.collection: Written together with consent_status.

items.name: Account created (joined)
items.collection: Database default at insert.

items.name: Profile updated
items.collection: Default at insert. No trigger or code updates it later.

items.name: Consent record id
items.collection: Database default.

items.name: Student id
items.collection: The signed-in student.

items.name: Consent answer
items.allowed: granted | declined | withdrawn ('withdrawn' is never written)
items.collection: One row per answer given in the consent dialog.

items.name: Consent text version
items.collection: The version constant of the consent text shown.

items.name: Consent answer time
items.collection: Database default.

items.name: Session id
items.collection: Created by the extension at sign-in or at restore after VS Code starts.

items.name: Student id
items.collection: The signed-in student.

items.name: Course id (unused)
items.collection: Leftover from the dropped course tables.

items.name: Session start
items.collection: Database default when the extension creates the row.

items.name: Last activity flush
items.collection: Set to now by every activity flush that has something to write (every 3 minutes while the editor is in use).

items.name: Session end
items.collection: Declared in the base schema. No code writes it.

items.name: Extension version
items.allowed: version from the extension manifest, e.g. '0.2.0'
items.collection: Read from package.json at activation.

items.name: VS Code version
items.collection: vscode.version at session creation.

items.name: Operating system
items.collection: process.platform at session creation.

items.name: Active coding time
items.collection: Heartbeat model: each edit, selection change, editor change or save is a heartbeat while the window has focus. The gap to the previous heartbeat is added when it is 2 minutes or less. Summed per flush.

items.name: Lines written
items.collection: Sum of new line breaks in document edits (file scheme only). Undo and redo are excluded. An edit event that adds or removes more than 20 lines is ignored.

items.name: Lines deleted
items.collection: Sum of removed line spans in document edits, with the same exclusions as lines_written.

items.name: Files created
items.collection: Count of files created through VS Code (onDidCreateFiles). Files created in the terminal or by other tools are not seen.

items.name: Languages edited
items.allowed: object: VS Code languageId -> count of counted edit events, e.g. {"python": 42}
items.collection: Each edit event that counts toward lines_written/lines_deleted adds 1 to its document languageId. Merged by addition per key.

items.name: Fixed without asking
items.collection: DiagnosticTrigger compares the error and warning list of an open document before and after each settle cycle. A diagnostic that disappears and was never asked about adds 1.

items.name: Help offers shown
items.collection: Adds 1 the first time a "What does this mean?" gutter icon is drawn for a diagnostic in the active editor (at most 3 per document). Pruned when the diagnostic goes away, so a returning error counts again.

items.name: Large pastes
items.collection: One edit event with exactly one content change that adds more than 20 lines and removes at most 1 line. A heuristic: VS Code has no paste flag.

items.name: Large paste lines
items.collection: Sum of added lines of the edits counted in large_paste_count.

items.name: Left VS Code
items.collection: Adds 1 each time the VS Code window loses focus.

items.name: Time away from VS Code
items.collection: Length of each completed absence (window unfocused, then focused again), capped at 10 minutes per absence. An absence that never ends is not counted.

items.name: Saves
items.collection: Adds 1 for each document save event.

items.name: Debug runs
items.collection: Adds 1 for each debug session started in VS Code.

items.name: Task runs
items.collection: Adds 1 for each VS Code task started. A program typed into the terminal is not a task and is not seen.

items.name: New errors right after a fix
items.collection: Diagnostics that appear in a document in the same settle cycle as a resolution there, or within 60 seconds after one.

items.name: Edits while an unaided error was present
items.collection: For each diagnostic counted in errors_resolved_without_asking, the number of edits to its document between the offer being shown and the diagnostic going away (0 when no offer was shown).

items.name: Breaks
items.collection: Adds 1 when the gap between two heartbeats is longer than 2 minutes.

items.name: Switched between files
items.collection: Adds 1 when the active editor changes to a different file (file scheme).

items.name: Files opened
items.collection: Number of distinct files that became the active editor in this extension host. Assigned (not added) at each flush.

items.name: Question id
items.collection: Database default.

items.name: Session id
items.collection: Sent by the extension. explain does not check that the session belongs to the caller.

items.name: Student id
items.collection: Taken from the JWT by explain.

items.name: Course id (unused)
items.collection: Leftover from the dropped course tables.

items.name: Question time
items.collection: Database default when explain inserts the row (after the model answered or the cache was hit).

items.name: Trigger source
items.allowed: check: diagnostic | runtime | selection | stuck | paste | success. Only 'diagnostic' and 'selection' are produced.
items.collection: 'diagnostic' for help on an error or warning, 'selection' for help on selected code (or the cursor area).

items.name: Where the question started
items.allowed: diagnostic_codelens | diagnostic_lightbulb | diagnostic_gutter_hover | selection_codelens | selection_lightbulb | selection_status_bar | selection_keybinding | sidebar_button | command_palette | null
items.missing: null = not recorded (older rows, or a value explain did not recognise)
items.collection: Each button, link or shortcut passes its own value. explain stores null for an unknown value.

items.name: Question type
items.allowed: what_does_this_mean | what_does_this_do | why_works | whats_wrong | simpler_example | free_text (no database check)
items.collection: 'what_does_this_mean' for every error question. For selections: the preset picked in the question list; the sidebar button and the command palette use 'what_does_this_do' without asking.

items.name: Student's own question
items.collection: Typed by the student after choosing "Something else…". The only student-written text that is stored.

items.name: Selected lines
items.missing: null for error questions and for questions asked with no selection
items.collection: end line - start line + 1 of the selection when the student asked.

items.name: Selected characters
items.missing: null in the same cases as selection_line_count
items.collection: Length of the selected text.

items.name: Error message
items.allowed: first diagnostic message, cut to 500 characters, or null
items.collection: The message of the first diagnostic sent with the request, as the compiler or linter wrote it.

items.name: Normalized error message
items.collection: error_signature with every digit run replaced by #, quoted strings replaced by "X", trimmed and lower-cased (normalizeErrorSignature). Null before migration 0004.

items.name: Error source (tool)
items.collection: vscode.Diagnostic.source of the first diagnostic.

items.name: Error code
items.collection: vscode.Diagnostic.code of the first diagnostic, as a string.

items.name: Error severity
items.allowed: error | warning (information | hint are possible values but never offered), or null
items.collection: Severity label of the first diagnostic.

items.name: File name
items.collection: Base name of the document the question was about.

items.name: Waited after the offer
items.missing: null when no visible offer existed (selection questions, or a diagnostic past the 3-offer cap)
items.collection: Time from the first drawing of the gutter offer for this diagnostic to the click. Negative or malformed values are stored as null.

items.name: Edits before asking
items.missing: null in the same cases as help_latency_ms
items.collection: Number of edit events in the document between the offer being shown and the click.

items.name: Same error asked before
items.collection: Number of this student's earlier questions with the same error_signature_normalized, counted at insert time. 0 for selection questions.

items.name: Time since the same error
items.missing: null for the first occurrence and for selection questions
items.collection: Time from the student's latest earlier question with the same normalized error to now.

items.name: Concept
items.allowed: 2-40 characters, written by the model in the feedback language
items.collection: Short name of the general concept behind the question, part of the model's structured answer. Cached answers written before the field existed get 'unspecified'.

items.name: Same concept asked before
items.collection: Number of this student's earlier questions whose concept matches this one (case-insensitive), counted at insert time.

items.name: Question title
items.collection: 3-6 word title from the model's structured answer. Shown in the student's history list. 'Untitled' for old cached answers.

items.name: Explanation text (hint ladder)
items.allowed: {title, concept, confidence: high|low, needsMoreContext: bool, l0_decode, l1_locate, l2_concept: {rule, example}, l3_fix: {change, why}}
items.collection: The whole validated answer. On a degraded answer, l2_concept and l3_fix hold empty strings.

items.name: Hint depth (went to)
items.collection: Starts at 0 (L0 and L1 are shown together). record-level raises it to 2 when the student opens the rule and to 3 when they open the fix. It never goes down.

items.name: Helpful rating
items.collection: One click on "Was this helpful?" (Yes = 1, Not really = -1). Re-answering from a reopened explanation overwrites it.

items.name: Outcome (self-report)
items.collection: One click on "How did it go?" (Solved it / Still stuck).

items.name: Could do it alone
items.collection: One click on "Could you do this one yourself now?" (Yes / Maybe / Not yet).

items.name: Answered from cache
items.collection: true when an identical earlier answer was reused (same language, question type, normalized error and normalized code).

items.name: AI provider
items.allowed: provider id: openai | anthropic | gemini | openai_compatible (not the model name)
items.collection: Id of the provider that answered (the fallback provider when it was used). For cache hits, the provider of the cached answer.

items.name: Prompt tokens
items.collection: Input tokens reported by the provider (last successful pass).

items.name: Completion tokens
items.collection: Output tokens reported by the provider (last successful pass).

items.name: AI response time
items.collection: Time inside explain from before the first model call to after the last pass (includes a repair pass). Not the wait the student saw.

items.name: Event id
items.collection: Database sequence.

items.name: Session id
items.collection: Resolved by log-event from the interaction, or checked against the caller's own sessions.

items.name: Student id
items.collection: Taken from the JWT.

items.name: Question id
items.collection: Set for events about one question; null for session-level events.

items.name: Event type
items.allowed: post_feedback_edit | diagnostic_resolved | explanation_visibility | fix_undone | question_picker_abandoned | returned_to_code | feedback_abandoned | request_failed | file_cleared | feedback_language_changed | explanation_reopened | explanation_copied | run_finished | level_reached
items.collection: Allowlist in log-event (unknown type -> 422). level_reached is written by record-level only.

items.name: Idempotency key
items.collection: unique (user_id, client_event_id) makes a repeated once-per-question event a no-op.

items.name: Event payload
items.allowed: object; fields per event type (see event items)
items.collection: Derived measurements only, never code or typed text (file_cleared carries a file name).

items.name: Event time (named 'client')
items.collection: Set by the Edge Function with its own clock at insert time, not by the extension.

items.name: Event time (server)
items.collection: Database default at insert. Used by every dashboard query.

items.name: Opened a hint level
items.collection: Written by record-level each time the student opens L2 (rule) or L3 (fix).

items.name: Level opened
items.collection: 2 = rule, 3 = fix.

items.name: Raised the hint depth
items.collection: true when the level is above the stored max_level_reached.

items.name: Time from question to opening
items.collection: Server time now minus interactions.created_at.

items.name: Time on screen
items.collection: Reported when the next explanation replaces this one, or at VS Code shutdown.

items.name: Time on screen
items.collection: Total time the sidebar view was visible while this explanation was the current one.

items.name: On screen when it arrived
items.collection: Whether the sidebar view was visible when the explanation was delivered.

items.name: Back to the code
items.collection: After feedback is shown (L0+L1 on arrival, then L2, L3), the first text change or selection change in any editor within 10 minutes.

items.name: Level shown last
items.collection: 1 = the explanation (L0+L1), 2 = rule, 3 = fix.

items.name: Back to the code after
items.collection: Time from the feedback being shown to the first editor activity.

items.name: Left without acting
items.collection: No editor activity within 10 minutes of the last feedback shown, or VS Code closed first.

items.name: Level shown last
items.collection: As in returned_to_code.

items.name: Reason
items.collection: timeout = 10 minutes passed; session_end = the extension was shut down first.

items.name: First edit after the fix
items.collection: The first qualifying edit in the same document within 5 minutes after L3 was opened (not undo/redo, at most 20 added lines, not a pure deletion).

items.name: Similar to the suggested fix
items.collection: Jaccard overlap of lower-case word tokens ([a-z0-9_]+) of the inserted text and the l3_fix.change text.

items.name: Lines from the pointed line
items.collection: Distance in lines from the question focus line to the nearest edge of the changed range.

items.name: Undid the change
items.collection: An undo in the same document within 2 minutes after the edit measured by post_feedback_edit.

items.name: Copied from the explanation
items.collection: A copy command inside the explanation panel. Repeatable.

items.name: Copied from level
items.missing: null when the selection did not start inside a level block
items.collection: The level block where the copied selection starts. The copied text is not sent.

items.name: Opened again later
items.collection: The student clicked a card in the history list and the stored explanation was shown again. Repeatable.

items.name: Error gone after explaining
items.collection: The diagnostic the student asked about disappeared from the open document (compared by uri + line + message).

items.name: Time to error gone
items.collection: Time from the click on the offer to the diagnostic disappearing.

items.name: Time the error was present
items.missing: absent when no offer was shown for this diagnostic
items.collection: Time from the offer first being shown to the diagnostic disappearing.

items.name: Edits while the error was present
items.missing: absent when no offer was shown
items.collection: Edit events in the document between the offer and the disappearance.

items.name: File became error-free
items.collection: A document that had errors or warnings has none left (session-level event).

items.name: File name
items.collection: Base name of the document.

items.name: Time with errors
items.collection: Time from the first diagnostic in the episode to the last one going away.

items.name: Edits
items.collection: Edit events in the document during the episode.

items.name: Errors seen
items.collection: Diagnostics present at the start plus those that appeared later in the episode.

items.name: Asked about
items.collection: Clicks on "What does this mean?" in this document during the episode.

items.name: Run ended
items.collection: A VS Code task process ended (onDidEndTaskProcess). Programs typed into the terminal are not seen.

items.name: Exit code
items.collection: Exit code of the task process.

items.name: Ended without error
items.collection: exitCode === 0.

items.name: Closed the question picker
items.collection: The student opened the question list for a selection and closed it, or closed the own-question box, without asking.

items.name: Where it was closed
items.collection: preset = the list of questions; free_text = the box for an own question.

items.name: Where the picker was opened
items.collection: Same values as interactions.trigger_surface.

items.name: Selected lines
items.collection: As interactions.selection_line_count.

items.name: Selected characters
items.collection: As interactions.selection_char_count.

items.name: Failed request
items.collection: A help request failed after the student asked (timeout after 25 s, error from the server, or another error).

items.name: Failure kind
items.collection: timeout = no answer within 25 s.

items.name: Server error code
items.allowed: rate_limited | provider_error | provider_timeout | invalid_request | unauthenticated | ... (only when kind = backend)
items.collection: The error code returned by the Edge Function.

items.name: Retry after
items.collection: Seconds until the rate limit resets (rate_limited only).

items.name: Feedback language changed
items.collection: The student switched the feedback language while a session existed.

items.name: Previous language
items.collection: Language before the change.

items.name: New language
items.collection: Language after the change.

items.name: Cache entry id
items.collection: Database default.

items.name: Cache key
items.collection: sha256 of 'generic|na|language|questionType|normalized error|sha256(normalized code)'.

items.name: Course id (unused)
items.collection: Written as null.

items.name: Course week (unused)
items.collection: Written as null.

items.name: Answer language
items.collection: Feedback language of the request.

items.name: Error message
items.collection: Raw first diagnostic message (not cut).

items.name: Cached hint ladder
items.collection: The validated model answer.

items.name: AI provider
items.collection: Provider id, as in interactions.model_used.

items.name: Entry source
items.collection: Always written as 'generated'.

items.name: Times reused
items.collection: Raised by 1 on every cache hit (atomic RPC increment_explanation_reuse, since migration 0022; earlier hits were not counted).

items.name: Cache entry created
items.collection: Database default.

items.name: Student id
items.collection: Row created by the first non-cached answer.

items.name: Course id (unused)
items.collection: Never written.

items.name: Private learner notes
items.collection: Written by generate-summary in English, third person, for the model only. Sent inside every later explain request; never shown to the student.

items.name: AI learning summary
items.allowed: 20-700 characters, in the feedback language, or empty

items.name: Suggested practice
items.allowed: 10-400 characters, in the feedback language, or empty
items.collection: A short practice problem on the most repeated error or topic, written in the same model call.

items.name: Summary written at

items.name: New questions since the summary
items.collection: Raised by 1 for every non-cached answer (read-then-write). Reset to 0 by generate-summary.

items.name: Row updated
items.collection: Default at insert; set again only by the dashboard reset.

items.name: Student id
items.collection: The caller.

items.name: Hour window

items.name: Requests this hour
items.collection: Raised by 1 for each non-cached answer (read-then-write).

items.name: Tokens this hour
items.collection: prompt + completion tokens of each non-cached answer.

items.name: Single-row key
items.collection: Primary key that allows one row only.

items.name: Requests per hour
items.collection: Set by an admin in the dashboard.

items.name: Requests per day (UTC)
items.collection: Set by an admin in the dashboard.

items.name: Limits changed at

items.name: Limits changed by

items.name: Storage bucket course-materials
items.collection: Created in 0003. No code uploads or reads files.

items.name: Online now
items.formula: Distinct students with a coding_sessions started_at or last_seen_at, an interaction, or an event in the last 10 minutes. Ignores the period filter.

items.name: Active students
items.formula: Distinct students with any trace in the period: a session start, a session last_seen_at, a question, or an event.

items.name: New students
items.formula: profiles created in the period.

items.name: Questions
items.formula: Count of interactions created in the period. The previous period has the same length and ends where this one starts.

items.name: All-time questions
items.formula: Count of all interactions of the student, ignoring the period.

items.name: Active coding time
items.formula: Sum of coding_sessions.active_seconds over sessions started in the period.

items.name: Sessions
items.formula: Count of coding_sessions started in the period.

items.name: Session length (avg.)
items.formula: Mean of (last_seen_at - started_at) in minutes over sessions started in the period, 1 decimal.

items.name: Breaks per session (avg.)
items.formula: Mean of idle_gap_count over sessions started in the period, 1 decimal.

items.name: Active days
items.formula: Distinct calendar dates of coding_sessions.started_at in the viewer's time zone, over sessions started in the period.

items.name: Last active
items.formula: Latest of: session started_at or last_seen_at, interaction created_at, event server_ts. All time.

items.name: Sessions without help
items.formula: Sessions started in the period with no interaction (by session_id) / sessions started in the period.

items.name: Hint was enough
items.formula: Questions with max_level_reached <= 1 / questions, in the period. Per student: solved_alone / questions (export column "Hint enough %").

items.name: How far students went into the hints
items.formula: Counts of questions in the period by max_level_reached: hint (<= 1), rule (= 2), fix (>= 3).

items.name: Error gone after explaining
items.formula: Diagnostic questions in the period with at least one diagnostic_resolved event / diagnostic questions in the period. Median of msToResolution of the first such event.

items.name: Did the error go away? (by hint depth)
items.formula: error_gone_pct and the median time, split by level = greatest(least(max_level_reached, 3), 1): 1 = L0-L1, 2 = L2, 3 = L3.

items.name: Fixed without asking
items.formula: Sum of coding_sessions.errors_resolved_without_asking over sessions started in the period.

items.name: Edits per unaided fix (avg.)
items.formula: sum(silent_resolution_edits) / sum(errors_resolved_without_asking) over sessions started in the period.

items.name: Rated helpful
items.formula: helpful_rating = 1 / (helpful_rating = 1 + helpful_rating = -1), questions in the period.

items.name: AI response time
items.formula: Mean latency_ms of questions in the period with latency_ms not null (cache hits excluded).

items.name: Response time (median)
items.formula: Median (p50) and 95th percentile of latency_ms, cache hits excluded.

items.name: Failed requests
items.formula: Count of request_failed events in the period; grouped by payload kind and code.

items.name: Failure rate
items.formula: failures / (questions + failures) in the period.

items.name: Answered from cache
items.formula: cache_hit = true / questions in the period (also per provider).

items.name: Tokens used
items.formula: Sum of prompt_tokens and completion_tokens in the period; also per time bucket and per provider.

items.name: Usage limits today
items.formula: Per student, from usage_counters: requests in the current UTC hour, requests and tokens since 00:00 UTC. Top 10.

items.name: Needs attention
items.formula: Students with at least one reason in the period: repeat_error = max(recurring_error_count) >= 2 (same error 3+ times); still_stuck = any self_reported_outcome 'still_stuck'; needs_fix = questions >= 5 and fix (max_level_reached >= 3) >= 70% of them; many_attempts = at least 2 questions with edits_before_ask and mean edits_before_ask >= 8; unhelpful = 2+ ratings of -1; inactive = last activity more than 7 days ago (all time). Sorted by number of reasons.

items.name: Asked for help when offered
items.formula: Per ISO week (Monday, viewer time zone): 100 x diagnostic questions created that week / sum(diagnostics_offered) of sessions started that week, capped at 100; null when no offers.

items.name: Hint was enough (weekly)
items.formula: Per ISO week: 100 x questions with max_level_reached <= 1 / questions created that week; null when no questions.

items.name: Sessions without help (weekly)
items.formula: Per ISO week: 100 x sessions started that week with no interaction / sessions started that week; null when no sessions.

items.name: Asked again
items.formula: Questions in the period with recurring_error_count > 0.

items.name: Asked again within 10 minutes
items.formula: Questions in the period with ms_since_previous_same_error <= 600000.

items.name: Edits before asking (avg.)
items.formula: Mean of edits_before_ask (non-null) over questions in the period, 1 decimal. The class view uses the median instead.

items.name: Waited after the offer (median)
items.formula: Median of help_latency_ms (non-null) over questions in the period.

items.name: On screen when it arrived
items.formula: Questions with an explanation_visibility event where visibleAtDelivery = true / questions with any explanation_visibility event.

items.name: Time on screen (median)
items.formula: Median visibleMs over explanation_visibility events of questions asked in the period.

items.name: Back to the code after (median)
items.formula: Median msToReturn over returned_to_code events of questions asked in the period.

items.name: Opened L2 after (median)
items.formula: Median msSinceCreated over level_reached events with level = 2.

items.name: Opened L3 after (median)
items.formula: Median msSinceCreated over level_reached events with level = 3.

items.name: Left without acting
items.formula: Distinct questions (asked in the period) with a feedback_abandoned event.

items.name: Opened again later
items.formula: Distinct questions (asked in the period) with an explanation_reopened event.

items.name: Copied from it
items.formula: Distinct questions with an explanation_copied event; copied_by_level counts events by payload level ('L0'-'L3' or 'unknown').

items.name: Edited the code (after the fix)
items.formula: Distinct questions with a post_feedback_edit event.

items.name: Within 2 lines of the pointed line
items.formula: Questions with post_feedback_edit where editedLineDistance <= 2 / questions with post_feedback_edit.

items.name: Similar to the suggested fix (avg.)
items.formula: round(100 x mean(overlapRatio)) over post_feedback_edit events.

items.name: Undid the change
items.formula: Distinct questions with a fix_undone event.

items.name: Closed the question list without asking
items.formula: Count of question_picker_abandoned events in the period, split by payload stage ('preset', 'free_text').

items.name: Where questions start
items.formula: Questions in the period grouped by trigger_surface (null shown as 'unknown').

items.name: Running the code
items.formula: total = run_finished events in the period; success = payload success true; after_explanation = runs with a question in the same session created in the 15 minutes before; plus their success share.

items.name: Error questions by severity
items.formula: Diagnostic questions in the period grouped by lower(error_severity) ('unknown' when null).

items.name: Languages edited
items.formula: Top 6 language ids by summed language_counts over sessions started in the period.

items.name: Recurring concepts
items.formula: Top 5 concepts of the student in the period, grouped by lower(trim(concept)).

items.name: Concepts students ask about most
items.formula: Top 12 concepts in the period (grouped case-insensitively): questions, distinct students, questions that reached the fix.

items.name: Most common errors
items.formula: Top 12 errors in the period keyed by 'error_source error_code' when present, otherwise error_signature_normalized: questions, distinct students, questions that reached the fix.

items.name: When students work
items.formula: Counts by ISO weekday (1-7) x hour (0-23) in the viewer's time zone: questions by created_at, sessions by started_at.

items.name: Does confidence hold up?
items.formula: For each post_confidence answer (yes, maybe, no) on questions in the period: total, and asked_again = questions for which the same student later asked a question with the same error_signature_normalized or the same concept (case-insensitive), at any later time.

items.name: Files worked through
items.formula: Latest 25 file_cleared events in the period with their payload fields.

items.name: Work habits (totals)
items.formula: Sums over sessions started in the period: focus_loss_count, unfocused_seconds, editor_switch_count, files_visited, files_created, save_count, debug_session_count, task_run_count, large_paste_count, large_paste_lines; and count of feedback_language_changed events.

items.name: Explanations asked for (student panel)
items.formula: Count of all interactions of the student (all time).

items.name: Errors you worked out yourself (student panel)
items.formula: Count of interactions with max_level_reached <= 1 (all time). The student still asked for an explanation.

items.name: Days using this (student panel)
items.formula: Distinct calendar dates of coding_sessions.started_at in the student's computer time zone (all time).

items.name: Total active time, lines, files, fixed without asking (student panel)
items.formula: All-time sums over coding_sessions: active_seconds (shown in hours, 1 decimal), lines_written, lines_deleted, files_created, errors_resolved_without_asking.

items.name: Summary progress bar
items.formula: min(hours since summary_generated_at / 24, interactions_since_update / 3), capped at 1. A new summary is requested at 1.

items.name: Dependency trend report (SQL)
items.formula: Per student and UTC week of the session start: help offers, diagnostic questions of those sessions, fixed_unaided, pct_offers_taken (not capped), pct_resolved_at_explanation, mean_edits_per_unaided_fix.

items.name: Question type vs resolution report (SQL)
items.formula: Per question_type: total, max_level_reached <= 1, = 2, >= 3, and % resolved at the explanation.

items.name: Session rhythm report (SQL)
items.formula: Per student and week: sessions, mean session minutes, mean active minutes, mean breaks, sessions by part of day (06-11, 12-17, 18-23, 00-05) using the database time zone.

items.name: Sessions without help report (SQL)
items.formula: Per student: sessions, sessions with no interaction, % without help, errors fixed unaided, help offers.

items.name: Summary rewrite rule
items.formula: A new summary is written when 24 hours have passed since summary_generated_at AND interactions_since_update >= 3, or at once (force) after a feedback language change. The model sees the last 30 questions (title, outcome), days active, the resolution pattern, question types and the most frequent normalized error when it appears 3+ times.

issues.text: Consent is recorded but not enforced. The code and the consent text say that declining turns telemetry off, but no code checks consent_status before writing coding_sessions counters, events or the research columns of interactions. Students who declined, and students who closed the dialog (pending), are recorded like everyone else.
Withdrawal is promised in the consent text and the README but not implemented. consent_log.status 'withdrawn' is never written, and there is no withdraw command or function (addendum §9).

The consent text says the extension sends 'your course context' (no course context exists) and does not mention continuous editor activity (active time, lines, focus changes, pastes, saves, runs, file names). The README lists only part of this activity.

Trigger sources 'runtime', 'stuck', 'paste' and 'success' are allowed by the database check but never produced. There is no run/crash capture, no stuck detection and no paste trigger; runOutput is never sent. Only 'diagnostic' and 'selection' exist.

'Programs run' is not shown to students (addendum §15). Runs are observed only as VS Code tasks (task_run_count, run_finished with exit code) and debug sessions. The dashboard subtitle 'Runs in the terminal' is misleading: a program typed into the terminal is not seen.
interactions.model_used and explanations.model_used hold the provider id (openai, anthropic, gemini, openai_compatible), not the model name. The dashboard already notes this.
events.client_ts is set by the Edge Function clock at insert time, not by the extension. There is no client-side event time.
max_level_reached is 0, 2 or 3. L0 and L1 appear together, so 1 is never written. The dashboard groups <= 1 as "Hint only (L0-L1)".

Columns or objects never written or never read: profiles.display_name, profiles.ui_language (always 'en' but shown in the dashboard), profiles.updated_at, coding_sessions.ended_at, the four course_id columns, explanations.week_no, explanations.source (always 'generated'), learner_profiles.updated_at, the concept_vocabulary table, and the course-materials storage bucket.
A click on the selection gutter-icon link passes no surface, so it is stored as 'selection_keybinding'. 'Selection: shortcut' therefore mixes the keyboard shortcut and the gutter link.
question_type 'what_does_this_do' is both a chosen preset and the default for the sidebar button and the command palette (no question list is shown). Use trigger_surface to separate them.

A diagnostic is identified by file + line + message. When an unrelated edit moves an error to another line, the code sees one error resolved and a new one appearing. This can inflate errors_resolved_without_asking, follow_on_error_count and diagnostic_resolved. The code comments accept this.

diagnostics_offered counts only gutter offers drawn in the active editor (max 3 per document), while errors_resolved_without_asking counts every error or warning that disappears, including those never offered. The two are not on the same base. The dashboard caps "Asked for help when offered" at 100%.

A coding_sessions row is created at every sign-in or restore in each VS Code window (a reload or a second window starts a new one). ended_at is never set and last_seen_at moves only on non-empty 3-minute flushes. Empty sessions exist and raise "Sessions without help"; session length is a lower bound.
'Active days' has three definitions: the dashboard uses the viewer's time zone, the student panel uses the student's computer time zone, and generate-summary uses the server clock (UTC).
interactions_since_update grows only with non-cached answers, so cached answers do not count toward the next summary.

The read-only SQL reports and the dashboard use different formulas for similar measures: dependency_trend.sql puts questions in the week of their session start (UTC) and does not cap at 100; the dashboard uses the question's own week in the viewer's time zone and caps. session_rhythm.sql uses the database time zone, although its comment says the student's clock.

The three self-report answers have no timestamp, and they can be given again when the explanation is reopened from the history list. The last answer overwrites the earlier one, so the time of answering is unknown.

RLS lets every signed-in student read all rows of explanations (policy: course_id is null). The cached answers and raw error messages were generated for other students' code. There is no user id, but code fragments can appear. Raise with the data protection review.

Stored text that can hold personal information: free_text (the student's words), file names (interactions.file_name, file_cleared.fileName), raw error messages (they quote identifiers and literals from the code), ladder_payload (model text can quote code) and the learner summaries. The dashboard export includes username, free text, file name and error.

The only identity is the username the student types at first sign-in. A new or mistyped username silently creates a new account. There is no course code, student number, GitHub sign-in or separate internal id.
There is no flag for test, developer or teacher accounts.
explain does not check that sessionId belongs to the caller (known gap in supabase/CLAUDE.md).

SPEC_ADDENDUM §15 says the history list shows 20 rows and three numbers; the code shows 10 rows and eight numbers. §9 (withdrawal), §10 (background summarizer) and followup_turns describe things that were never built or were removed.
The Overview "Active students" counts research events as activity; the daily sheet of the export does not.
The last explanation's dwell time and 'session_end' abandonment are sent during shutdown, fire-and-forget. They are often lost when VS Code closes or crashes.
returned_to_code fires on the first text or selection change in any editor or document, not only the file of the question.
The model fields confidence and needsMoreContext are stored only inside ladder_payload. gatingDegraded is not stored; it can be inferred from an empty l2_concept.rule.
latency_ms is measured inside explain (model time, including a repair pass). It is null for cache hits and is not the wait the student experienced.
The dashboard calls the weekly composite 'Independence trend' (TR 'Bağımsızlık eğilimi', ES 'Tendencia de autonomía'). The site uses these labels.

Two similar names measure different things. 'Errors you worked out yourself' (student panel) counts questions where the student asked but did not open the rule or fix. 'Fixed without asking' counts errors that disappeared without any question.

recurring_concept_count uses a case-insensitive pattern match on the model-written concept. Paraphrases ('loop bounds' vs 'loop limits') count as different concepts.

"Most common errors" (dashboard_insights) and the export column "Error" group errors by concat_ws(' ', error_source, error_code). concat_ws skips a null code, so an error with a source but no rule code (all Pylance syntax errors) gets the key 'Pylance' instead of falling back to its message. Every such error is counted under one row labelled "Pylance".
